newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up on electronics boost.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up on electronics boost.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended higher on Friday as investors defied a Wall Street's overnight selloff and bought heavily on fundementally strong electronics shares, brokers said.
The benchmark stock index finished 29.99 points or 0.37 percent higher to T$8,119.70.
Turnover was an active T$137.8 billion.

Electronic led the gains, rising a sharp 2.85 percent to make up for slack trading in other sectors, including the battered food sector, still reeling from a hog farm epidemic and pork export ban that erupted a week ago, brokers said.

"The sharp rise reflected the strong fundementals underlying electronic shares. Dow Jones' planned inclusion of seven Taiwan shares in its Taiwan index showed some effect, too," said analyst Amy Huang of Nomura Securities.

Three of the seven Taiwan stocks to be added by Dow Jones from April 1 are electronic shares -- Acer Peripherals, which rose T$0.5 to T$88.5, motherboard maker Asustek Computer which gained T$22 to T$635 and monitor maker Inventec, which rose T$6 to T$286.

Of the other Dow Jones additions, Kuo Yang Construction gained T$1 to T$73 and footwear giant Pou Chen added T$5 to T$138. Taichung Business Bank and United World Chinese Commercial Bank ended unchanged despite a 0.57 percent slide in financial issues.
Brokers said Friday's rise gave hopes for renewed momentum after a 600-point correction that followed the hog disease outbreak and two handsome rebounds on Wednesday and Thursday.
"Investors now are more concerned about the performance of a company and choose to buy shares with solid fundamentals," said Oliver Fang of National Securities.
